messages:
customer_acme: Hi team — starting ~2026-03-17T08:15:00Z we saw a wave of 500s and a lot of truncated responses for EU traffic. App retried and our bill jumped unexpectedly. Example trace id: trc_8f3a2c. sample curl we hit: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_***' -H 'x-region: eu' -d '{"model":"redwood/pro/1.2","prompt":"Summarize..."}'`
maria_support: Sorry about that — digging in now. Can you confirm roughly how many failures and whether the responses were cut off (looks like half-sentence)? Also do you have a request id from one error?
customer_acme: ~120 errors in 12m, lots of responses end with "..." or "[TRUNC]". One req id: req_20260317_eu_91f. Billing page shows +92% tokens that hour.
ben_oncall: I see the trace. Routing shows EU requests hit eu-standby-02. The client asked for `redwood/pro/1.2` but runtime loaded `redwood-lite-v0.3` as a fallback. That variant has a different tokenizer/vocab — explains truncation and odd tokens.
carol_runtime: Confirming logs: `2026-03-17T08:14:52Z ModelLoad success: redwood-lite-v0.3 (quantized)` then `TokenizerWarning: unknown token conversion > replaced with <unk>` then `Response truncated due to token limit mismatch`. Relevant snippet: ```json
{"route_meta":{"requested_model":"redwood/pro/1.2","served_model":"redwood-lite-v0.3","fallback_trigger":"region_unavailable","region":"eu-west-1"}}
``` 
maria_support: How did the fallback pick a lite/quantized build? Shouldn't fallback be to a compatible architecture variant?
carol_runtime: It picked based on model family tag mismatch. The catalog entry for pro/1.2 had an absent 'capabilities' flag for eu-standby pool, so smart-routing matched by family prefix only and returned the nearest available model (lite) which is not capability-compatible. We're patching matching logic.
dave_billing: Billing note: retries + additional tokens from repeated partial responses accounted for the spike. Need a provisional credit while we investigate. Can ops/eng provide token counts for req range trc_8f3a2c -> req_20260317_eu_91f?
erin_cs: I'll coordinate with the customer on a temporary workaround. Maria — can we suggest a per-API-key fallback disable or a hard model pin for ACME?
maria_support: Yes — short-term mitigation: customer can pin `model=redwood/pro/1.2` and set header `x-fallback-policy:fail` to avoid auto-fallback to incompatible variants. Example: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_ACME' \
  -H 'x-fallback-policy:fail' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/pro/1.2","prompt":"..."}'
```
This will return an explicit error instead of serving a downgraded model.
ben_oncall: We also have a quicker platform toggle: for that customer id we can set routing override to force EU-primary region for next 24h while we patch catalog. Will do now. @deploy-bot can you apply `routing.override(customer_id=acme-corp,region=eu-primary,ttl=86400)`?
deploy-bot: routing.override applied to acme-corp -> eu-primary (ttl=86400) :white_check_mark:
carol_runtime: Engineering action items: (1) patch catalog matching to include capability-compatibility and tokenizer-vocab fingerprinting (PR queued) (2) add guard in smart-router to avoid selecting quantized/lite variants when requested_model has pro capability flag (3) backfill quick inventory of regions with mismatched model families.
maria_support: Customer asked for repro steps so they can validate post-fix. Carol — can you paste a minimal repro they can run that reliably shows the mismatch (so they can confirm it's serving the right/ wrong model)?
carol_runtime: Repro (will reproduce if standby pickable):
```
# 1) normal request (may succeed)
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_***' -H 'x-region: eu' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/pro/1.2","prompt":"generate 200 tokens of lorem"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/completions
# look for response header X-Served-Model: redwood-lite-v0.3 -> indicates fallback
```
maria_support: For the billing ask, Dave — please open a billing incident and tag it `support:critical` and attach counts. We'll provisionally credit the token overage while engineering confirms root cause.
dave_billing: Created INC-20260317-0891, tagging and putting hold on extra charges for acme-corp until we complete root cause.
erin_cs: I'll update the customer now with: (a) temporary routing override applied, (b) workaround header to fail instead of fallback, (c) billing incident opened, (d) ETA for fix ~ 4-8 hours for catalog tag patch and a hotfix to router.
customer_acme: Thanks. We'll test with the fail header and let you know. Appreciate the quick response.
carol_runtime: Postmortem notes (to be formalized): primary cause = incomplete model metadata in catalog (missing capability/tokenizer fingerprint) + router greedy matching by family prefix allowed a quantized lite variant pick. Preventive: add stricter matching + unit tests that simulate region failover and assert tokenizer compatibility.
maria_support: Follow-ups: I'll create a support ticket with logs you provided, schedule a sync for +1 after fix, and include a summary for the billing team. Closing note: please escalate if any new errors after the override expires. :thumbsup:
